questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: The pearl problem is meant to show that sample sizes fall as:
questions.explanation: Lower RMM or higher materiality → higher planned DR → smaller n.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Identifying and assessing RMM includes performing risk assessment procedures and obtaining an understanding of:
questions.explanation: First box: obtain an understanding of the company and its environment.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Understanding the company and its environment includes relevant industry, regulatory, and other external factors; the nature of the company; the company’s accounting principles; objectives and strategies; and:

choices.text: The company’s measurement and analysis of its financial performance
The number of referred-to auditors worldwide

questions.explanation: Also: structure/personnel, capital sources, investments, size/complexity, sources of earnings, key suppliers/customers; significant accounting changes, competencies, judgment, controversies, odd transactions, new laws; measures used in contracts/compensation, by outsiders, and by insiders.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: The RMM identification slide also lists obtaining an understanding of ICFR, considering information from client acceptance and retention, and:

choices.text: Setting sample size before understanding the company

questions.explanation: RAP, company/environment, ICFR, acceptance/retention information, analytical procedures. Later: team discussion regarding RMM and inquiry of the audit committee.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Analytical procedures are an evaluation of financial information made by a study of:

choices.text: Plausible relationships among both financial and nonfinancial data

questions.explanation: AP: plausible relationships among financial and nonfinancial data.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Planning analytical procedures are designed to enhance understanding of the client’s business and:

choices.text: Identify areas that might represent specific risks (unusual transactions, amounts, ratios, and trends)
Test operating effectiveness of every control

questions.explanation: Enhance understanding; identify risk areas.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: In performing AP, the auditor should develop an expectation about plausible relationships and compare it to relationships from recorded amounts. Differences could indicate:

choices.text: That materiality is too high by definition
That IR is chosen by the auditor

questions.explanation: Unexpected differences can indicate RMM.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Data analytics, per Byrnes et al. 2017 as quoted, is discovering and analyzing patterns, identifying anomalies, and extracting other useful information in data underlying or related to the subject matter of an audit through analysis, modeling, and visualization for the purpose of:
questions.explanation: Quoted definition: planning or performing the audit.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Using data analytics in risk assessment, the slides list: plan the procedure, access and prepare the data, consider relevance and reliability, perform the procedure, and evaluate results (identify notable items). Evaluating results can lead to identification of previously unidentified risk, modification of or support for the RMM assessment, and:

choices.text: Automatic issuance of an adverse opinion
Information to better design audit procedures to address RMM
A requirement to use Turnbull instead of COSO

questions.explanation: Three outcomes of notable items: new risk, change/support RMM, better-designed procedures.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: After RAP, company/environment, ICFR, acceptance/retention info, and AP, the auditor should also:

choices.text: Skip the team meeting if the client is large
Conduct a team discussion regarding RMM and inquire of the audit committee
Compute Joe’s n before understanding the business

questions.explanation: Team discussion on RMM; inquire of the AC.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: The auditor should identify and assess RMM at:

choices.text: The financial statement level and the assertion level

questions.explanation: FS level and assertion level.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: In identifying and assessing RMM, the auditor should identify risks using RAP information and characteristics of accounts/disclosures, literally ask “What could go wrong?”, determine whether the risks are pervasive, determine what kinds of misstatements could occur, assess likelihood and magnitude, identify significant accounts/disclosures and relevant assertions, and:

choices.text: Determine whether any of the risks are significant risks
Treat every account as clearly trivial

questions.explanation: End by identifying significant risks that need special audit consideration.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Risk factors for identifying significant accounts, disclosures, and relevant assertions include size and composition of the account, susceptibility to misstatement, volume/complexity/homogeneity of transactions, nature of the account, accounting complexities, exposure to losses, contingent liabilities, related-party transactions, and:

choices.text: Changes from the prior period in account and disclosure characteristics
Whether the ticker has four letters
The number of audit-committee meetings last decade

questions.explanation: Evaluate qualitative and quantitative risk factors on line items and disclosures, including period-to-period changes.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: A significant risk is one that requires special audit consideration because of the nature of the risk, its likelihood, and:

choices.text: The sample size in Joe’s example

questions.explanation: Nature, likelihood, and potential magnitude.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Factors used to identify significant risks include whether the risk is a fraud risk; relation to recent significant economic, accounting, or other developments; complexity of related transactions; related parties; high accounting complexity/judgment/uncertainty; significant unusual transactions; and:

choices.text: Whether the stock pays a dividend
The effect of the quantitative and qualitative risk factors used in identifying significant accounts/disclosures
The number of specialists on the tax team only

questions.explanation: Start from the same qualitative/quantitative factors used for significant accounts, then layer fraud, developments, complexity, related parties, judgment, unusual transactions.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: The slides ask who chooses audit risk and float the auditor, the market, the profession, and the courts. Regardless of that discussion, the operational definition used in the ARM is:

choices.text: The risk of losing the client
The risk the auditor may unknowingly fail to appropriately modify the opinion on FS that are materially misstated
The risk that controls are costly
The risk that materiality is a percentage

questions.explanation: Same AR definition as Module 6, now plugged into IR × CR × DR.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: RMM in the ARM is:
questions.explanation: RMM = IR × CR. AR = RMM × DR.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: The auditor does not choose IR or CR; the auditor:

choices.text: Assesses them and then solves for planned DR
Sets them equal to 5% by policy

questions.explanation: Assess IR and CR; calculate planned DR; then set NTE of substantive work.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: “The nature of the company” in the understanding slide includes structure and personnel, capital sources, investments, size/complexity, sources of earnings, and:
questions.explanation: Nature of the company: structure/personnel, capital, investments, size/complexity, earnings sources, key suppliers/customers.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Understanding the company’s accounting principles includes significant changes, accounting competencies, use of judgment, accounting controversies, accounting for odd transactions, and:

choices.text: The number of walkthroughs in Module 8

questions.explanation: Accounting principles understanding includes new laws and regulations.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Performance measures the auditor should understand include measures for contractual commitments or compensation arrangements, measures used by outsiders, and:

choices.text: Measures used by the PCAOB to grade the firm
Measures used by insiders to monitor performance

questions.explanation: Contracts/compensation, outsiders, and insiders’ monitoring measures.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: If planned DR is high because RMM is low, the pearl math and the strategy slides agree that the auditor can:

choices.text: Accept less persuasive evidence / a smaller sample, all else equal
Skip the understanding of the company

questions.explanation: High planned DR = you can live with a higher chance of missing a remaining misstatement = less persuasion / smaller n.

questions.module: Module 7: The Audit Risk Model and Inherent Risk
questions.prompt: Identifying significant accounts is not a purely quantitative size test because the slide tells you to evaluate:

choices.text: Only whether the account exceeds materiality
Qualitative and quantitative risk factors related to the line items and disclosures

questions.explanation: Qualitative and quantitative risk factors — size, susceptibility, complexity, related parties, changes, etc.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Internal control, on the Module 8 definition slide, is a process effected by an entity’s board of directors, management, and other personnel, designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding achievement of objectives in specified categories. That wording matches:

choices.text: The COSO-style definition of internal control

questions.explanation: Process; effected by BOD, management, and other personnel; reasonable assurance; objectives in the COSO categories (operations, reporting, compliance).

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977 books-and-records/internal-accounting-control provisions listed on the slide include transactions executed in accordance with management’s authorization, prompt recording in the correct amount/accounts/period, access to assets only with authorization, and:

choices.text: A required ICFR opinion for every issuer in 1977
Recorded assets compared with existing assets at reasonable intervals, with appropriate action for differences

questions.explanation: FCPA 1977: authorization, recording, restricted access, and periodic comparison of recorded vs. existing assets.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: FDICIA 1991, as described, applies to financial institutions with assets over:
questions.explanation: Over $500 million. Management assessment of controls over financial reporting and regulatory compliance; the bank considers its own standards; the assessment must be audited by an external auditor; report filed with regulators.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: SOX Section 302, in the 10-K and 10-Q, requires the CEO/CFO to certify (among other things) responsibility for IC, that they designed and maintained IC properly, evaluated effectiveness, reported conclusions, designed controls so material information is made known to them, disclosed significant IC deficiencies to the auditor and AC and material weaknesses in ICFR to the auditor, disclosed fraud by anyone with a significant role in IC, and:

choices.text: Disclosed to the auditor any significant changes in IC

questions.explanation: 302 certifications include significant IC changes, plus the deficiency/MW/fraud disclosures listed on the slide.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: SOX Section 404, in the 10-K, requires the CEO/CFO to state responsibility for ICFR and:

choices.text: Omit any assessment if the auditor agrees
Contain management’s assessment of ICFR effectiveness (and have the assessment and IC audited)

questions.explanation: 404: responsibility + management assessment of effectiveness, with the assessment and IC audited.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: AS 2201 describes ICFR as a process designed by the CEO and CFO and effected by the board, management, and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of GAAP financial statements, including policies that pertain to maintenance of records reflecting transactions and dispositions of assets, reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded to permit GAAP FS and that receipts/expenditures are authorized, and reasonable assurance regarding:

choices.text: Prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of company assets that could have a material effect on the FS
FDICIA’s $500 million test for all issuers

questions.explanation: AS 2201 ICFR definition ends with safeguarding of assets that could materially affect the FS.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: SEC rules require management to base its ICFR evaluation on a suitable, recognized control framework established by a body that followed due-process procedures, including broad distribution for public comment. Examples on the slide are COSO and:

choices.text: The Turnbull Report (FRC Internal Control Revised Guidance for Directors on the Combined Code, October 2005)

questions.explanation: Recognized framework; examples: COSO and Turnbull.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor should obtain an understanding of each COSO component of ICFR. If management uses another acceptable framework:

choices.text: The auditor must force a switch to COSO

questions.explanation: Understand each component of the framework actually used; components may differ if not COSO.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: In the control environment, the auditor gains an understanding of whether effective ICFR is promoted. In risk assessment, the auditor understands management’s process for identifying risks of misstatement, assessing the likelihood of resulting misstatements, and:

choices.text: Deciding how to respond to risks

questions.explanation: COSO risk assessment: identify risks, assess likelihood of misstatements, decide how to respond.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Understanding information and communication includes classes of significant transactions; how transactions are initiated, authorized, processed, recorded, and reported (and related documentation and the role of IT); methods/data/assumptions/specialists for estimates; and:
questions.explanation: Don’t skip the period-end reporting process.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor gains an understanding of control activities to assess the factors that affect control risk and to:

choices.text: Select the COSO framework for management

questions.explanation: Control activities understanding → assess CR factors and design further procedures. Monitoring: activities to monitor ICFR effectiveness and how corrections are initiated.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Walkthroughs can be used to help understand the flow of transactions, evaluate the design of controls, and determine whether those controls have been:
questions.explanation: Walkthroughs: understand the flow, evaluate design, determine implementation.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: In a walkthrough, at points where important processing procedures occur, the auditor questions company personnel about their understanding of prescribed procedures and controls in order to understand the process, identify points at which a necessary control is missing or not designed effectively, and:

choices.text: Gain an understanding of the different types of significant transactions handled by the process
Issue the ICFR opinion that day

questions.explanation: Three walkthrough aims at those points: understand the process, spot missing/poorly designed controls, understand transaction types.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor’s objective in an ICFR audit is to express an opinion on the effectiveness of ICFR. Because ICFR cannot be considered effective if one or more material weaknesses exist, the auditor must plan and perform the audit to obtain appropriate evidence sufficient for reasonable assurance about whether material weaknesses exist:

choices.text: For the entire three-year period in the 10-K
As of the date specified in management’s assessment
Only as of the prior year-end
On a quarterly rolling basis only

questions.explanation: As of the date specified in management’s assessment.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: A material weakness in ICFR may exist even when financial statements are not:
questions.explanation: MW can exist even if the FS are not materially misstated.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: AS 2201 ICFR audit procedures: the audit should be integrated, apply a top-down approach, assess fraud via controls over unusual transactions, period-end journal entries, related-party transactions, accounting estimates, and management incentives to manipulate the FS, and:
questions.explanation: Integrated, top-down, fraud-related controls, use of others.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: A top-down approach includes assessing entity-level controls, identifying and assessing risk in significant accounts and assertions (the same ones as the FS audit), understanding likely sources of misstatement (walkthroughs; ask “what can go wrong”), and selecting controls to test — only:

choices.text: Every control in the COSO appendix

questions.explanation: Only essential controls. Under AS 2 (which preceded AS 2201), many auditors felt obligated to test many redundant or unnecessary controls.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Entity-level controls on the slide include the control environment (management’s philosophy/operating style, integrity and ethical values, board/AC oversight), controls over management override, the company’s risk assessment process, centralized processing and controls, monitoring of operations and of other controls (including internal audit, the AC, and self-assessment programs), controls over the period-end financial reporting process, and:

choices.text: Policies that address significant business control and risk management practices

questions.explanation: Last bullet: policies addressing significant business control and risk management practices.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: To understand likely sources of potential misstatements and select controls to test, the auditor should understand the flow of transactions for relevant assertions (initiated, authorized, processed, recorded), verify identification of points at which a misstatement could arise, identify controls that address those potential misstatements and controls over unauthorized acquisition/use/disposition of assets, and:

choices.text: Understand how IT affects the company’s flow of transactions

questions.explanation: Include IT’s effect on the flow of transactions.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: For each control tested, the auditor must evaluate design effectiveness and operating effectiveness. Design effectiveness asks: if operated by persons of authority and competence, would the control prevent or detect a material misstatement? Walkthroughs that include inquiry, observation, and document inspection are ordinarily:

choices.text: Sufficient to evaluate operating effectiveness for the whole year

questions.explanation: Walkthroughs (inquiry, observation, inspection) are ordinarily sufficient for design. Operating effectiveness asks: is the control operating as designed?

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Key design-evaluation considerations include control purpose (preventive or detective), level of aggregation, consistency of performance, correlation with the relevant assertion, criteria for investigation (detective controls), precision of expectations (entity-level controls), whether the control is manual or automated, dependency on information produced by the entity, competence and authority of the person performing the control, and:

choices.text: The number of pearls in Joe’s bag

questions.explanation: The last bullet on that design list is dependence on other controls.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: When testing operating effectiveness, key considerations are risk, the nature of testing (inquiry, observation, inspection of documentation, reperformance), the extent of testing (more extensive → more evidence), the timing of testing (interim vs. after the balance-sheet date), and potential control changes. Interim testing creates:

choices.text: A roll-forward period between the testing date and the balance-sheet date

questions.explanation: Interim testing ⇒ roll-forward period. Roll-forward considerations include the risk of related accounts/assertions, the specific control and whether it may no longer be effective, planned reliance, sufficiency of interim evidence, and the length of the remaining period.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: A control deficiency exists when design or operation of a control does not allow management or employees, in the normal course of duties, to prevent or detect misstatement on a timely basis. A material weakness is a deficiency (or combination) such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the FS will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. A significant deficiency is:

choices.text: More severe than a material weakness
Less severe than a material weakness, yet important enough to merit attention of those charged with oversight of ICFR

questions.explanation: Three-tier: deficiency → significant deficiency → material weakness. “Reasonable possibility” = reasonably possible or probable under FAS 5.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Severity of a deficiency considers whether there is a reasonable possibility a control will fail to prevent/detect misstatement and the magnitude of the potential misstatement, plus nature of the deficiency, magnitude for annual and interim FS, existence of redundant or compensating controls, and:

choices.text: Whether the ticker is four letters
Whether a prudent official would reach a different conclusion

questions.explanation: Prudent-official test is on the severity slide.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Written representations from management in an ICFR audit include acknowledging responsibility for ICFR, that management performed an evaluation using specified criteria, that management did not use the audit as part of the basis for its assessment, management’s conclusion on effectiveness, disclosure of all deficiencies, description of fraud that resulted in a material FS misstatement or that involved senior management or management with an ICFR role, whether deficiencies have been resolved, and subsequent changes in ICFR. Failure to obtain the representations is:

choices.text: Immaterial if the opinion is unqualified on the FS

questions.explanation: No written representations → scope limitation.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Under AS 2201 reporting, report all ICFR deficiencies in writing to management. Report all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in writing to management and the audit committee — and to the board if:

choices.text: The audit committee is judged ineffective
The opinion on the FS is unqualified

questions.explanation: SD and MW → management and AC; also the board if the AC is ineffective.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: If there is a material scope limitation on the ICFR audit, the auditor must:

choices.text: Disclaim an opinion on internal controls (“except for” opinions are not allowed)
Issue an unqualified ICFR opinion with an explanatory paragraph

questions.explanation: Any material scope limitation → disclaimer. Except-for opinions are not allowed on ICFR.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor should modify the ICFR report if management’s annual report elements are incomplete or improperly presented, there is a scope restriction, the auditor refers to other auditors as a partial basis, there is other information in management’s ICFR report, or:

choices.text: The company changed auditors two years ago

questions.explanation: Appendix C conditions include a misstated 302 certification.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Howard Electric evaluates ICFR using Turnbull instead of COSO. Based on the slides, that is:

choices.text: Acceptable if Turnbull is a suitable recognized framework that followed due process
A scope limitation requiring a disclaimer

questions.explanation: The criteria slide explicitly lists Turnbull as an example recognized framework. Using it is not, by itself, a problem.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor identifies a significant deficiency. Management’s ICFR report does not discuss it. Under the reporting rules on the slides:

choices.text: The ICFR opinion must be adverse
SDs are reported in writing to management and the AC; management’s public ICFR report is about effectiveness/MWs, not a requirement to discuss every SD
This is a FAS 5 probable loss

questions.explanation: SD → written communication to management and AC. Public ICFR opinion/report centers on whether ICFR is effective (i.e., whether MWs exist), not on listing every SD.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Management identifies a material weakness, describes it in detail in its ICFR report, and the auditor agrees. The ICFR opinion is:
questions.explanation: MW (and management agrees) → adverse ICFR opinion. The slide’s reporting grid: MW and management agrees / MW and management doesn’t / no MW / scope limitation.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor identifies four ICFR deficiencies, but the probability of a material misstatement due to them is remote. Those deficiencies are:

choices.text: Not material weaknesses, because MW requires a reasonable possibility (reasonably possible or probable under FAS 5), not a remote likelihood

questions.explanation: Remote ≠ reasonably possible/probable.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor identifies a material weakness; management disagrees and refuses to modify its ICFR report. The auditor’s ICFR report should:

choices.text: Be modified because a MW exists and management’s report does not agree

questions.explanation: MW + management doesn’t agree → modify. (Adverse opinion on ICFR plus language about the disagreement/inadequate management report.)

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: KLM’s auditor cannot test controls over estimation of the fair value of a material investment, but found no other ICFR deficiencies. This is:

choices.text: A scope limitation; a material scope limitation requires a disclaimer, and except-for opinions are not allowed
Irrelevant because the FS may still be fairly stated

questions.explanation: Inability to test controls over a material area is a scope limitation. Disclaimer if material; no except-for.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor finds a material misstatement that management refuses to correct and plans a qualified opinion on the FS. For ICFR, a material misstatement that was not prevented or detected is ordinarily evidence of:

choices.text: A material weakness (even though the FS opinion may be qualified)

questions.explanation: An uncorrected material misstatement implies ICFR did not prevent or detect it → MW. MW can exist even when you also modify the FS opinion.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: The auditor finds a material misstatement; management corrects it before issuance; the FS opinion is unqualified. The ICFR implication is:

choices.text: ICFR must be effective because the FS are now correct
A MW may still exist — a MW in ICFR may exist even when the financial statements are not (or are no longer) materially misstated

questions.explanation: The Module 8 objective slide: MW may exist even when FS are not materially misstated. Correction before issuance does not erase the control failure.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Reno describes a capital-lease MW in vague terms. The auditor agrees a MW exists. The problem is:

choices.text: Management’s report elements are incomplete/improperly presented (vague description), which is a condition for modifying the auditor’s ICFR report

questions.explanation: Appendix C: modify if management’s annual report elements are incomplete or improperly presented.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: During substantive testing of revenue, the auditor finds the controller intentionally recorded three 2019 sales for 2020 shipments. That is fraud by someone with a significant role in IC, which SOX 302 says must be disclosed to the auditor, and it is strong evidence of:

choices.text: A material weakness and a fraud risk involving management with an ICFR role
A reason to skip written representations

questions.explanation: Intentional premature revenue by the controller → fraud / ICFR failure, typically MW, and 302/representation implications.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Management’s SOX 302 certification is misstated; the auditor reports this to management and the AC; neither responds appropriately. The auditor should:

choices.text: Ignore it if the FS are fairly stated
Modify the ICFR report (Appendix C includes a misstated 302 certification) and consider communication/governance implications

questions.explanation: Misstated 302 certification is an explicit modify condition. Non-response by management/AC is a governance red flag on top of that.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Before issuing the report, the auditor identifies a subsequent event that does not relate to conditions existing at the ICFR evaluation date but does materially impact ICFR effectiveness going forward. This is:

choices.text: Always a MW as of year-end
A subsequent event that does not change the as-of-date opinion in the same way as a condition that existed at the evaluation date, but it can require disclosure/report treatment as a subsequent event

questions.explanation: The assignment flags a subsequent event not relating to conditions at the evaluation date but affecting ICFR going forward — treat as a subsequent event, not automatically as an as-of-date MW.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: In the sales-process case, Risk #1 is “all orders shipped are not recorded as revenue.” The relevant assertion is:
questions.explanation: Shipped-but-not-recorded is completeness. The case marks it not a significant risk and not a fraud risk.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Control #1 automatically records sales and generates invoices when goods are scanned/released in Warehouse K. It does not rely on IPE, is automated, and is evaluated as a preventive control at the transaction level. Planned operating-effectiveness testing at interim is:

choices.text: A test of one, following one transaction through the system, plus ITGCs (including program-change controls) to confirm no changes since the prior year

questions.explanation: Automated control → test of one + ITGCs. Roll-forward: inquire of controller and IT manager about subsequent events/changes.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Risk #2 is “revenue is recorded for orders not shipped or fictitious sales.” The relevant assertion is existence or occurrence. The case marks it as:

choices.text: A significant risk and a fraud risk

questions.explanation: Existence/occurrence of fictitious or unshipped sales is a significant fraud risk in the case.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Control #2 is a daily warehouse-director review of the Orders Shipped & Invoiced Report. It relies on IPE (the report from Warehouse K), is manual and detective, and because OE depends on accuracy and completeness of IPE the team will test ITGCs, report logic, and source-data controls. Planned OE testing is:

choices.text: A test of one at 9/30 only

Select 40 days during the year (including some within two weeks of the balance-sheet date), inspect evidence of review, inquire, reperform, and check timely sign-off — apportioned through the year so no separate roll-forward is needed
Monthly budget-to-actual at a $4 million threshold

questions.explanation: 40 days, including near year-end; inspect, inquire, reperform, timely review. Because testing is spread through year-end, no extra roll-forward.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Risk #3 is inaccurate quantities/prices on shipped orders. The relevant assertion is:
questions.explanation: Quantities and prices → valuation/allocation. Not a significant risk and not a fraud risk in the case.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Control #3 is a monthly controller review of the reporting package at the operations meeting, investigating differences > $4 million or fluctuations > 15% vs. prior year or budget. Materiality in the case is $5 million, so the control is described as sufficiently precise. IPE includes the monthly package (PeopleSoft query; test GITCs) and the budget (test the budget process directly). Planned testing includes inquiry and inspecting meeting minutes for two months, then:

choices.text: A test of one automated invoice
Roll-forward by selecting a Q4 month and repeating the procedures

questions.explanation: Interim: inquiry + two months of minutes. Roll-forward: one Q4 month, same procedures.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Control #1 is classified as preventive because:

choices.text: Automation records revenue when goods ship, preventing shipped goods from going unrecorded
The warehouse director initials a report the next day
The controller reviews budget variances monthly

questions.explanation: Preventive = stops the error from occurring. Detective (#2 and #3) identifies after the fact.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Control #2 involves judgment with no specific dollar threshold, but the case still concludes it is sufficiently precise because all transactions are evaluated, the business is cyclical/predictable, and:

choices.text: The warehouse director has long tenure and knowledge of unusual customer/quantity patterns

questions.explanation: Precision can come from a knowledgeable daily transaction-level review, not only from a dollar threshold.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Which pairing of risk → assertion → control type matches the case?

choices.text: Risk 1 completeness / automated preventive; Risk 2 existence / manual detective daily; Risk 3 valuation / monthly detective analytics
All three are automated preventive completeness controls
All three are fraud-significant existence controls
Risk 3 is a completeness walkthrough only

questions.explanation: That mapping is the case: completeness+automated; existence+daily detective+IPE; valuation+monthly review with quantitative thresholds.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: AS 2 preceded AS 2201. The top-down slide’s point about AS 2 is that many auditors felt obligated to:

choices.text: Test many redundant or otherwise unnecessary controls

questions.explanation: AS 2201’s top-down, essential-controls approach is a reaction to that AS 2 experience.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: “Integrated” in AS 2201 means the ICFR audit and the financial-statement audit:

choices.text: Must be done by different firms
Should be performed as an integrated audit

questions.explanation: Integrated audit; significant accounts and assertions are the same for FS and ICFR.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: If there is no material weakness, the ICFR report (assuming no other modify conditions) is:
questions.explanation: Reporting grid: no MW → clean ICFR opinion (subject to Appendix C). MW → adverse. Scope limitation → disclaimer.

questions.module: Module 8: Auditing Internal Control over Financial Reporting
questions.prompt: Entity-level examples that monitor other controls include activities of the internal audit function, the audit committee, and:
questions.explanation: Monitoring of other controls: IA, AC, self-assessment programs.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: AS 1000, as quoted, says the objective of the ordinary audit is the expression of an opinion on the fairness with which the FS present, in all material respects, financial position, results of operations, and cash flows in conformity with GAAP. The auditor must plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the FS are free of material misstatement, whether caused by:
questions.explanation: Reasonable assurance as to material misstatement from error or fraud.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: The financial statements are management’s responsibility. The auditor’s responsibility is to express an opinion. Management is responsible for adopting sound accounting policies and for establishing and maintaining internal control that will initiate, record, process, and report transactions consistent with:

choices.text: Management’s assertions embodied in the financial statements

questions.explanation: IC should produce transactions consistent with management’s assertions in the FS.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Bell et al. 2005, as quoted, describe the audit as a process of:
questions.explanation: Evidence-driven, belief-based, risk assessment.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: The overall purpose of auditing, on the Module 9 purpose slide, is to lend the auditor’s credibility to financial statements that would otherwise be untrustworthy due to:

choices.text: Conflicts of interest inherent in the corporate form

questions.explanation: Conflicts of interest in the corporate form make unaudited FS untrustworthy; the audit lends credibility.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Planned DR is calculated at the financial statement level and at the assertion level. Planned DR = AuR / (IR × CR) = AuR / RMM. The auditor addresses RMM (and achieves planned DR) through appropriate overall audit responses and:
questions.explanation: AS 2301: overall responses plus specific procedures.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Overall audit responses listed include assigning responsibilities appropriately, providing appropriate supervision, being unpredictable (test other things, vary timing, vary testing thresholds, be unannounced, vary locations), evaluating accounting principles, making pervasive changes to overall audit strategy, and:
questions.explanation: Be skeptical is the last overall response on the slide.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Specific audit procedures should be designed to address the specific risks identified. As RMM increases, obtain:
questions.explanation: As RMM increases, more persuasive evidence. Also consider the type of misstatements that could occur because of the risk.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Evidence is all the information used by the auditor in arriving at the conclusions on which the auditor’s opinion is based — the information accumulated through audit procedures. The objective is to plan and perform the audit to obtain appropriate audit evidence that is sufficient to:

choices.text: Support the opinion expressed in the auditor’s report

questions.explanation: Appropriate and sufficient evidence to support the opinion.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Evidence sufficiency is a quantity determined by RMM and by the quality of collected evidence. All else equal, as risk increases, the necessary quantity of evidence:
questions.explanation: Higher risk → more quantity. Higher quality evidence → less corroborating quantity needed.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: As the quality of evidence increases, the necessary quantity of corroborating evidence:

choices.text: Must equal n in Joe’s example

questions.explanation: Better quality reduces the quantity of corroboration needed.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Evidence appropriateness is a quality determined by relevance (the relationship between the evidence and the assertion being tested) and reliability, which depends on the source of the evidence, including:

choices.text: The length of the workpaper filename
Level of source bias and level of source competence
Whether the evidence was filed on EDGAR

questions.explanation: Reliability: source, source bias, source competence.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Non-substantive procedures include planning activities, risk assessment, reporting procedures, and tests of controls. Substantive procedures are activities performed to detect material misstatement or fraud at the assertion level and include tests of details of balances (or transactions) and:
questions.explanation: TOC are not substantive. Substantive = TOD + substantive AP.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Tests of details evaluate account balances by testing the individual elements that comprise the balance. Examples on the slide include bank accounts making up cash, customer accounts/invoices making up AR, inventory items, prepaid insurance policies, and vendor amounts making up AP. Because balances often comprise many elements, tests of details often require:
questions.explanation: TOD often require sampling — which is why Module 9 is titled Evidence and Audit sampling, even though these 11 slides stop at introducing TOD/sampling and the expanded ARM.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: The expanded audit risk model on slide 11 is AuR = IR × CR × AP × TD, where AP is the risk that substantive analytical procedures will not detect a material misstatement that occurred and was not prevented/detected by ICFR, and TD is the risk that tests of details will not detect a misstatement that occurred, got through ICFR, and:

choices.text: Was not detected by the auditor’s substantive analytical procedures

questions.explanation: TD is residual after IR, CR, and AP. Rearranged: TD = AuR / (IR × CR × AP).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: In the expanded ARM, Planned DR is split into:

choices.text: Substantive analytical procedures risk (AP) and tests of details risk (TD)

questions.explanation: Planned DR = AP × TD.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: If the auditor wants a given AuR and assesses high IR and CR, then to hold AuR the product AP × TD must be:

choices.text: Lower (more substantive work, more persuasive TOD/AP evidence)

questions.explanation: AuR = IR × CR × AP × TD. High IR×CR forces low AP×TD — i.e., stronger substantive AP and/or TOD.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a substantive procedure on these slides?

choices.text: A test of details of the AR balance
Testing the individual insurance policies in prepaid insurance

questions.explanation: Tests of controls are listed as non-substantive, along with planning, risk assessment, and reporting procedures.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Unpredictability as an overall response includes testing other things, varying timing, varying testing thresholds, being unannounced, and:

choices.text: Telling the client the full sample in advance

questions.explanation: Vary locations is on the unpredictability list.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Relevance of evidence is the relationship between the evidence and:
questions.explanation: Appropriateness = relevance (to the assertion) + reliability (source/bias/competence).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Sufficiency is about quantity; appropriateness is about quality. The necessary quantity rises with RMM and falls as:
questions.explanation: Quantity needed falls when quality rises.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: An overall audit response that is about people, not procedures, is:

choices.text: Assign responsibilities appropriately and provide appropriate supervision
Tests of details of inventory items
The TD factor in the expanded ARM

questions.explanation: Assign responsibilities; supervise. Those sit with skepticism, unpredictability, evaluating accounting principles, and pervasive strategy changes.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Specific procedures should consider the type of misstatements that could occur due to the risk — the same “what could go wrong” idea as Module 7/8 — because evidence must be:

choices.text: Relevant to the assertion implied by that type of misstatement

questions.explanation: As RMM rises, more persuasive evidence; match procedures to the type of misstatement / assertion.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: The cash balance comprised of various bank accounts plus currency and coin is the slide’s example that tests of details:

choices.text: Always test only the total, never the parts
Test the individual elements that comprise the balance
Are the same as tests of controls

questions.explanation: Cash = bank accounts + cash on hand; AR = customers/invoices; inventory = items; etc.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Rearranging the expanded ARM, TD =
questions.explanation: TD = AuR / (IR × CR × AP). If AP is more effective (lower AP), allowable TD can be higher — less TOD, all else equal.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence and Audit Sampling (slides 1–11)
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly ties Modules 7 and 9 together using only these slides?

choices.text: Tests of controls are a component of planned DR in the expanded ARM
Planned DR from the ARM is achieved through overall responses plus specific procedures; the expanded model splits planned DR into AP and TD (substantive work), while IR × CR remain RMM
Sufficiency replaces relevance when RMM is high
Sampling is required for every walkthrough

questions.explanation: AR = RMM × DR = IR × CR × AP × TD. Overall responses + specific procedures (TOD and substantive AP) are how you hit planned DR. TOC are non-substantive and live in CR/RMM, not in AP×TD.
